name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Do a daily 15-minute manual crawl of the top 20% most-linked pages—those driving 80% of traffic—using the simplest browser extension that logs every link it sees. It’s fast, visible, and gives us immediate coverage gains without touching fragile automation. The trade-off is we miss deep, rare links, but those won’t block the bus task and we can revisit them once the gate is open.

name: Scriv
text: Manual crawl misses the 20% of links that drive the other 20% of traffic—those rare but critical pages break the access gate. Simpler: run a one-time, full-site crawl with a lightweight tool like Screaming Frog, then focus the daily 15-minute crawl on the top 20% to catch fresh additions. Settle it by comparing the cost of a single full crawl against the risk of missing those 20% of links.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a one-time full-site crawl with Screaming Frog, then switch to daily 15-minute manual crawls of the top 20% pages. This closes the 20% gap in link coverage immediately while keeping the daily work simple and visible. The trade-off is the upfront time and tool cost of the full crawl, but it’s a one-time hit that secures the access gate faster than incremental manual work alone.

name: Sift
text: The one-time full crawl with Screaming Frog isn’t a real solution—it’s a bandage. The real risk is that the site changes faster than we can crawl it, so the snapshot becomes stale before we even start the daily work. Settle it by running the full crawl *once*, then switching to a lightweight, automated crawler (like Sitebulb) for daily checks—it’s still simple, but it catches fresh links without manual labor.

name: Scope
text: Run a one-time full-site crawl with Screaming Frog, then switch to daily 15-minute manual crawls of the top 20% pages. This closes the 20% gap in link coverage immediately while keeping the daily work simple and visible. The trade-off is the upfront time and tool cost of the full crawl, but it’s a one-time hit for permanent coverage gains.

name: Scriv
text: The one-time Screaming Frog crawl is a snapshot, not a system. The real risk is that the site evolves daily, so yesterday’s full coverage becomes tomorrow’s blind spot before the next crawl even starts. Settle it by running the full crawl once, then switching to a lightweight, automated daily crawler that only checks for new links on the top 20% pages—no manual work, no stale snapshots.
